newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI revises down 96/97 capital spending.
newsitem.headline: DDI revises down 96/97 capital spending.

text.p: Japanese telecoms firm DDI Corp said on Thursday it had revised down its group capital spending for the year to March 31 to 350 billion yen from the original plan of 404 billion yen announced last November.

A DDI spokesman said the reduction was due in part to lower-than-expected costs for constructing basic stations used in mobile communications. Some investments were postponed until the next business year, he said.
"We have not changed our plan to continue investment in infrastructure," he said.
Depreciation costs for the year were revised down to 118.4 billion yen from 126.1 billion yen.
DDI earlier boosted its 1996/97 profit forecast after an agreement with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp to reduce NTT's interconnection charges.
